sections.title: Describing things that get done without naming the agent
sections.content: Hungarian rarely uses true passive verb forms in everyday speech. Instead, Hungarian creates mediopassive verbs with the suffix *-ódik / -ődik*. These verbs indicate that an event happens or gets settled on its own, without focusing on who performs the action: *megoldódik* (gets resolved/works out), *befejeződik* (comes to an end/finishes), *elintéződik* (gets sorted out).

sections.title: Active verb vs. Mediopassive form
rows: comes to an end / wraps up (befejez → befejeződik)

items.spanish: Bízom benne, hogy a félreértés hamar megoldódik.
items.english: I trust that the misunderstanding will soon be resolved.
The important tasks are gradually getting settled.

items.spanish: A heti megbeszélés egy óra múlva befejeződik.
items.english: The weekly meeting will conclude in an hour.

sections.content: Notice that the grammatical subject is the thing undergoing the process (e.g. *a probléma*, *a projekt*), and the verb takes ordinary intransitive third-person singular/plural agreements (*megoldódik / megoldódnak*).
